source.title: A feedback neural circuit for calibrating aversive memory strength

confidence_rationale: Predictive cues recruit a descending CeA -> vlPAG feedback circuit that inhibits aversive teaching signals to LA; optogenetic inhibition of this pathway disinhibits predicted aversive responses in LA and resets fear learning. Causal evidence that the conditioned threat predictor itself gates its own teaching signal (a closed-loop PE), supporting MECH-599's event-taught store and its extinction/saturation behaviour.
failure_signatures: When the predictive cue's feedback to PAG is blocked, predicted shocks teach again and learning resets; a threat store without a prediction-driven suppression of its own teaching signal would never saturate and would over-learn.

mapping.source_claim_statement: Predictive sensory cues recruit a descending feedback circuit from the central amygdala that activates a population of vlPAG pain-modulatory neurons to control aversive memory strength; inhibiting this pathway disinhibits predicted aversive responses in LA neurons and resets fear learning levels.
mapping.ree_translation: MECH-599's store should be taught by aversive-PE events; this paper shows how biology computes that PE: the store's own prediction feeds back to suppress the teaching signal. For a V3 build this argues the store's output should also be what subtracts from its teacher (a closed loop), rather than a separate PE computed elsewhere.
mapping.mapping_caveat: Rat, footshock, optogenetics. Concerns memory strength and saturation, not cue specificity. The CeA->PAG route is an output of the threat system being used for teaching-signal control, which REE has no analogue of yet.
mapping.source_context: Rat; single-unit LA recording; optogenetic inhibition of CeA->vlPAG projections during fear conditioning

confidence_components.notes: High-quality causal circuit work from the Johansen lab, follows 2010 paper. Mapping moderate.
